result.title: Rank Measures of Fine-Tuning Updates Need a Noise Baseline
result.comment: 24 pages, 6 figures, 15 tables. Under review at TMLR
result.summary: Studies of what fine-tuning does to a language model often summarise the weight update $ΔW$ by its rank. We compare the rank measures used for this against the same measures on a random matrix of the same shape, and against two harder references: the pretrained weights, and matched fine-tunes without alignment content. Measures that count directions put our fine-tuning updates only a little below noise; stable rank, computed from the same singular values, puts them far below. Both are right: an update has a few strong directions on top of a long tail. The pattern holds for thirteen released pairs up to 8B parameters, and it is not a mark of alignment: with training held fixed, instruction data does not stand out from Wikipedia or code, DPO gives the same update whether its preference labels are real or half swapped at random (one model, modest preference strength), and scrambled text gives the most concentrated update of all. Applied to a recent claim that post-training is superficial because the effective rank of the weights barely changes, the baselines show that a random update of the same size leaves that rank almost unchanged while wrecking the model, and that an edit built on the effective rank of the update has no measurable effect in our tests. Rank measures of weight updates need a noise baseline, and claims about alignment need a control without alignment content.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将微调权重更新 ΔW 的秩类度量与同形状随机矩阵基线、预训练权重以及去掉对齐内容的匹配微调相比较，覆盖十三对最大 8B 的模型，并据此质疑「后训练因权重有效秩几乎不变而只是表面改变」的结论。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「秩与有效秩度量必须配噪声基线和内容匹配控制」的论证思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中如何判断 latent 状态或训练更新携带的信息是否超出随机噪声，以及贡献分配的诊断是否可靠；但对象是纯文本 LLM 的权重更新，与推理期视觉状态的联系需人工判断。
